Alright, let me think through this year. I'm 49, been on this land thirty years. Seven-point-eight mu isn't much — my oldest son works in Handan at a factory, sends money home, so we're not squeezed as tight as some. But still, every yuan on inputs I have to see come back.

I split the land like this: 3 mu on cotton in the western plot (sandy, does better there), and 4.8 mu on wheat-maize double crop on the better soil. That's how I've done it the last five-six years.

**Wheat** goes in around October 10th, after I get the maize off in late September. I'll use the semi-dwarf variety the seed shop has — Jimai or something similar, whatever's in stock. Extension guy a few years back told me 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I've seen my wheat yellow at jointing when I do that, so I go a bit heavier. I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before plowing, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress urea maybe 15 kg per mu around jointing in March. Irrigate three times — once before winter, once at jointing, once at flowering. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, not bad. Herbicide once in spring for the weeds.

**Maize** right behind the wheat, mid-June, no time to waste — I hire the combine for wheat and the neighbor's rotary tiller the same day if I can. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, about 80 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, then urea topdress at the big trumpet stage around 15-18 kg. If July-August is dry I'll irrigate once, maybe twice — pumping costs money though. Expect around 500 kg per mu.

**Cotton** is more work and honestly I'm thinking about giving it up, but prices held up last year so I'll do it again. Plant end of April after I get the plastic film down. Seed maybe 50 yuan per mu. Fertilizer lighter than maize — cotton doesn't need so much N or it just grows leaves. I'll spray for bollworm two-three times, can't avoid it. Pick by hand with my wife and mother-in-law from September through October. Tough work.

Labor mostly family — me, my wife, my mother helps during cotton picking. I hire the combine and tractor but that's it.
